arxiv-2202-12044.title: Robust Subthermionic Topological Transistor Action via Antiferromagnetic Exchange
arxiv-2202-12044.creator: Sagnik Banerjee, Koustav Jana, Anirban Basak, Michael S. Fuhrer, Dimitrie Culcer, Bhaskaran Muralidharan
arxiv-2202-12044.description: Abstract The topological quantum field-effect transition in buckled 2D-Xenes can potentially be engineered to enable sub-thermionic transistor operation coupled with dissipationless ON-state conduction. Substantive device design strategies to harness this will necessitate delving into the physics of the quantum field effect transition between the dissipationless topological phase and the band insulator phase.

arxiv-2310-11809.title: Characterizations of p p -groups whose power graphs satisfy certain connectivity conditions
arxiv-2310-11809.creator: Ramesh Prasad Panda
arxiv-2310-11809.description: Abstract Let Γ \Gamma be an undirected and simple graph. A set S S of vertices in Γ \Gamma is called a cyclic vertex cutset of Γ \Gamma if Γ − S \Gamma-S is disconnected and has at least two components containing cycles. If Γ \Gamma has a cyclic vertex cutset, then it is said to be cyclically separable.

arxiv-2408-05282.title: Two-Edge Connectivity via Pac-Man Gluing
arxiv-2408-05282.creator: Mohit Garg, Felix Hommelsheim, Alexander Lindermayr

arxiv-2409-18753.title: Enhancing Explainability in Multimodal Large Language Models Using Ontological Context
arxiv-2409-18753.creator: Jihen Amara, Birgitta König-Ries, Sheeba Samuel
arxiv-2409-18753.description: Abstract Recently, there has been a growing interest in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) due to their remarkable potential in various tasks integrating different modalities, such as image and text, as well as applications such as image captioning and visual question answering.

arxiv-2506-01177.title: Bridging Quantum and Classical Computing in Drug Design: Architecture Principles for Improved Molecule Generation
arxiv-2506-01177.creator: Andrew Smith, Erhan Guven
arxiv-2506-01177.description: Abstract Hybrid quantum-classical machine learning offers a path to leverage noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices for drug discovery, but optimal model architectures remain unclear. We systematically optimize the quantum-classical bridge architecture for generative adversarial networks (GANs) in molecular discovery using multi-objective Bayesian optimization. Our optimized model (BO-QGAN) significantly improves performance, achieving a 2.

arxiv-2507-22265.title: Cell-Probe Lower Bounds via Semi-Random CSP Refutation: Simplified and the Odd-Locality Case
arxiv-2507-22265.creator: Venkatesan Guruswami, Xin Lyu, Weiqiang Yuan
arxiv-2507-22265.description: Abstract A recent work (Korten, Pitassi, and Impagliazzo, FOCS 2025) established an insightful connection between static data structure lower bounds, range avoidance of NC 0 \text{NC}^{0} circuits, and the refutation of pseudorandom CSP instances, leading to improvements to some longstanding lower bounds in the cell-probe/bit-probe models.

arxiv-2511-09973.title: Difference Vector Equalization for Robust Fine-tuning of Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2511-09973.creator: Satoshi Suzuki, Shin’ya Yamaguchi, Shoichiro Takeda, Taiga Yamane, Naoki Makishima
arxiv-2511-09973.description: Abstract Contrastive pre-trained vision-language models, such as CLIP, demonstrate strong generalization abilities in zero-shot classification by leveraging embeddings extracted from image and text encoders. This paper aims to robustly fine-tune these vision-language models on in-distribution (ID) data without compromising their generalization abilities in out-of-distribution (OOD) and zero-shot settings.

arxiv-2511-19033.title: ReEXplore : Improving MLLMs for Embodied Exploration with Contextualized Retrospective Experience Replay
arxiv-2511-19033.creator: Gengyuan Zhang, Mingcong Ding, Jingpei Wu, Routong Liao, Volker Tresp, [6pt] LMU Munich, Munich Center for Machine Learning, TU Munich[6pt] gengyuan.zhang@lmu.de mingcong.ding@tum.de

Embodied exploration is a target-driven process that requires embodied agents to possess fine-grained perception and knowledge-enhanced decision making.

europmc-pmc5309787.creator: Schütte M, Risch T, Abdavi-Azar N, Boehnke K, Schumacher D, Keil M, Yildiriman R, Jandrasits C, Borodina T, Amstislavskiy V, Worth CL, Schweiger C, Liebs S, Lange M, Warnatz HJ, Butcher LM, Barrett JE, Sultan M, Wierling C, Golob-Schwarzl N, Lax S, Uranitsch S, Becker M, Welte Y, Regan JL, Silvestrov M, Kehler I, Fusi A, Kessler T, Herwig R, Landegren U, Wienke D, Nilsson M, Velasco JA, Garin-Chesa P, Reinhard C, Beck S, Schäfer R, Regenbrecht CR, Henderson D, Lange B, Haybaeck J, Keilholz U, Hoffmann J, Lehrach H, Yaspo ML.
europmc-pmc5309787.description: Colorectal carcinoma represents a heterogeneous entity, with only a fraction of the tumours responding to available therapies, requiring a better molecular understanding of the disease in precision oncology. To address this challenge, the OncoTrack consortium recruited 106 CRC...

europmc-pmc5743240.creator: Colles A.

pmc-10603109.title: Distribution of blaOXA-10, blaPER-1, and blaSHV genes in ESBL-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains isolated from burn patients
pmc-10603109.creator: Reem F Polse, Haval M Khalid, Wijdan M S Mero
pmc-10603109.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is resistant to a wide range of extended spectrum-lactamases (ESBLs) antibiotics because it produces several kinds of ESBLs. The goal of the current investigation was to identify the bacteria that produce extended spectrum -lactamases and the genes that encode three different ESBLs, such as blaOXA-10, blaPER-1 and blaSHV genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from burn patients.

pmc-11327246.title: Deep learning for detecting and characterizing oil and gas well pads in satellite imagery
pmc-11327246.creator: Neel Ramachandran, Jeremy Irvin, Mark Omara, Ritesh Gautam, Kelsey Meisenhelder, Erfan Rostami, Hao Sheng, Andrew Y. Ng, Robert B. Jackson
pmc-11327246.description: Methane emissions from the oil and gas sector are a large contributor to climate change. Robust emission quantification and source attribution are needed for mitigating methane emissions, requiring a transparent, comprehensive, and accurate geospatial database of oil and gas infrastructure. Realizing such a database is hindered by data gaps nationally and globally.

pmc-11459996.title: Crossfeat: a transformer-based cross-feature learning model for predicting drug side effect frequency
pmc-11459996.creator: Bin Baek, Hyunju Lee
pmc-11459996.description: BackgroundSafe drug treatment requires an understanding of the potential side effects. Identifying the frequency of drug side effects can reduce the risks associated with drug use. However, existing computational methods for predicting drug side effect frequencies heavily depend on known drug side effect frequency information. Consequently, these methods face challenges when predicting the side effect frequencies of new drugs.

pmc-11499992.title: Isolation, characterization, and assessment of Bacillus rugosus potential as a new probiotic for aquaculture applications
pmc-11499992.creator: Nermeen M. Shokrak, Nabilah Khairi, Nur Hazlin Hazrin-Chong, Radi A. Mohamed, Bahaa Abdella
pmc-11499992.description: Aquaculture is an important component of the world food supply and a significant source of protein. However, this industry faces numerous problems. Including poor fish feed digestion and uneconomic nutrient utilization. This can result in unsatisfactory growth rates and poor stock performance.

pmc-11716453.title: The Markers in Neuropsychiatric Disorders Study (The MiND Study): progress of a large nationwide Australian blood biomarker study and platform for collaborations to improve diagnosis and care of dementia and other brain conditions
pmc-11716453.creator: Dhamidhu Eratne, Courtney Lewis, Christa Dang, Jasleen Grewal, Matthew Kang, Henrik Zetterberg, Kaj Blennow, Alexander Santillo, Dennis Velakoulis, The MiND Study Group
pmc-11716453.description: BackgroundThe Markers in Neuropsychiatric Disorders Study (The MiND Study) is investigating the diagnostic and wider utility of blood based biomarkers such as neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and phosphorylated tau (p‐tau), as well as other markers, to improve timely and accurate diagnosis of dementia and distinction from non‐neurodegenerative and primary psychiatric disorder (PPD).

pmc-12472633.title: Perceptions Regarding Healthy Eating Based on Concept Mapping
pmc-12472633.creator: Gaeun Yeo, Jieun Oh
pmc-12472633.description: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to examine contemporary perceptions of healthy eating among individuals living in a rapidly evolving social, economic, and cultural environment. A mixed-methods approach was employed using the concept mapping method to collect, visualize, and analyze participants’ perceptions. Methods: Twenty-four Korean individuals aged 16 to 55 participated in the study.

pmc-13070331.title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Correlates of Multidrug-Resistant Uropathogens in Hospitalized Children
pmc-13070331.creator: Khitam Muhsen, Sama Haleem, Bshara Mansour, Ma’anit Shapira, Milena Pitashny, Mohammad Masarwa, Muna Omar, Wasef Na’aminh, Eias Kassem
pmc-13070331.description: PurposeAntibiotic resistance in uropathogens causing urinary tract infections (UTIs) is increasing; nonetheless, evidence on multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria remains limited. We aimed to examine the prevalence and risk factors of Gram-negative MDR bacteria in pediatric UTIs and compared the hospitalization duration and cost between patients with and without MDR.

pmc-13146104.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A716 LONGER ONSET-TO-DOOR TIMES IN NON-WHITE PATIENTS IN ITALY: A PROSPECTIVE, MULTICENTRIC STUDY ON 2402 PATIENTS
pmc-13146104.creator: Irene Scala, Pier Andrea Rizzo, Mauro Monforte, Andrea Zini, Anne Falcou, Massimo Del Sette, Maria Guarino, Anna Cavallini, Luisa Chiapparini, Maria Rosaria Bagnato, Vincenzo Andreone, Costanza Rapillo, Luigi Caputi, Marina Diomedi, Anna Bersano, Danilo Toni, Andrea Morotti, Simona Sacco, Paolo Cala
pmc-13146104.description: Background and aimsStudies from the USA have reported lower access to reperfusion treatments (RTs) for Ischemic Stroke (IS) among racial/ethnic minorities; however, evidence from Italy is lacking. We aimed to assess the impact of race/ethnicity on RTS administration and onset-to-door time (ODT).

pmc-13241643.title: Helminth infection dynamics in rehabilitating Javan slow lorises are driven by time since deworming rather than host traits
pmc-13241643.creator: Abdullah Langgeng, Marie Sigaud, Wendi Prameswari, Nur Purba Priambada, Puji Rianti, Richard Moore, Andrew JJ MacIntosh, Ikki Matsuda
pmc-13241643.description: Wildlife rehabilitation plays a central role in the conservation of threatened primates, yet parasite dynamics during captivity are rarely reported, particularly in relation to release readiness. We investigated gastrointestinal helminth infection patterns in rehabilitating Javan slow lorises (Nycticebus javanicus), a Critically Endangered species heavily impacted by the illegal wildlife trade.

pmc-13262918.title: CCB-4 and its sugar complexes induce mitotic catastrophe and p53-independent apoptosis through caspase-2 elevation and suppression of c-Myc in T47D cells
pmc-13262918.creator: Ni Putu Linda Laksmiani, Rohmad Yudi Utomo, Riris Istighfari Jenie, Yusuke Suenaga, Mitsunori Kirihata, Edy Meiyanto, Ratna Asmah Susidarti
pmc-13262918.description: Adding boron to curcumin analogs enhances their ability to inhibit cell growth and facilitates their detection within cells. Derivatives of diboronocurcumin are, therefore, promising options for cancer treatment. Our previous in silico analysis revealed that CCB-4 binds more tightly to proteins associated with breast cancer than Pentagamaboronon-0.

pmc-13325732.title: Preventive pharmacotherapy initiation after lipoprotein(a) measurement in low-risk adults
pmc-13325732.creator: Om A. Kothari, Kevin Maymi-Quintana, Rohan S. Ganti, Nicholas A. Bosch, Sheilah Bernard
pmc-13325732.description: ated Lp(a) confers cardiovascular risk independent of traditional lipid parameters such as low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) [[1], [2], [3], [4]]. Defined as ≥50 mg/dL (≥125 nmol/L), elevated Lp(a) affects approximately 20–25 % of the global population and represents a prevalent source of cardiovascular risk [2,5,6]. Unlike LDL-C, Lp(a) concentrations are minimally responsive to lipid-lowering therapies [3,6].

pmc-13412577.title: Purinergic and Energy Metabolism Disruption in Oxidative Stress-Mediated Immunotoxicity Induced by Aflatoxin B1 and Fumonisin B1
pmc-13412577.creator: Verónica S. Mary, Pilar A. Velez, Sol Quiroz, Sofía A. Díaz Iriso, Candelaria Amilibia, Héctor R. Rubinstein, Martín G. Theumer
pmc-13412577.description: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) and fumonisin B1 (FB1) are cereal-contaminating mycotoxins; co-exposure to these compounds is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma, although the underlying immunological mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of AFB1 and FB1, individually and combined, on immune cell function, focusing on Th1-associated cytokines, cytotoxic capacity, oxidative stress involvement, and energy and purinergic metabolism.

pmc-13421373.title: A Standards‐Based, Cloud‐Hosted CDS System for Gonorrhea Treatment and HIV Screening
pmc-13421373.creator: Edna Shenvi, Aziz Boxwala, Sarah Shaw, Andre Berro, Saugat Karki, Matthew Pooser, Jane E Yang, Gema Dumitru, Jeanne Ocampo, Amrita Tailor, Sanjat Kanjilal, Carlos Paredes, Ritche Hao, Nitu Kashyap, David Liebovitz, Alejandro Pérez

pmc-13518590.title: Assessment of brachial plexus and upper-extremity peripheral nerve injuries at the anatomical level using multimodal generative models
pmc-13518590.creator: Vincent G. J. Guillaume, Ron Martin, Jonas Roos, Robert Kaczmarczyk, Justus P. Beier, Benedikt Schäfer, Tim Leypold
pmc-13518590.description: IntroductionInjuries to the brachial plexus and its terminal branches can be devastating at the functional and occupational levels, as loss of even partial functions causes major disruptions in dexterity and mobility. The brachial plexus comprises multiple interconnected anatomical layers, making thorough anatomical knowledge essential for determining the extent of injury and the best treatment.

pmc-13619624.title: EPS deficiency aggravates intestinal mucosal inflammation and dysbiosis through disrupting macrophage polarization balance in ulcerative colitis
pmc-13619624.creator: Fengqin Zhu, Guiyuan Jin, Lihao Shi, Yufen Qin, Honglu Xue, Fengxian Dai, Xueying Chen, Guangxi Zhou
pmc-13619624.description: BackgroundUlcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disorder, and macrophages are essential for maintaining intestinal mucosal balance during UC. Long intergenic non-coding RNA–erythroid prosurvival (lincRNA-EPS) is a novel lincRNA identified as a key inflammatory regulator. Nonetheless, the specific role of EPS in the pathogenesis of UC remains unclear.
